subject: Performance SLO & VPC/on-prem network follow-up - Acme
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & VPC/on-prem network follow-up - Acme

Hi Alex / Priya - thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same view:

Summary of customer performance targets (from discussion):
- Latency: target P95 end-to-end inference latency <= 250 ms for streaming first-byte, P99 < 400 ms for typical requests.
- Throughput: baseline 100 requests/sec sustained, with burst up to 200 req/sec during peak.
- Concurrency: target 50 concurrent streaming sessions; typical session concurrency expected ~8 model tokens/sec per stream.
- Streaming: first-byte streaming (server-to-client) must start within 200-2300 ms, and keep sub-100 ms per-chunk streaming after initial byte for UX.

Private/VPC / on-prem network items we need to qualify before an internal perf test:
1) Network topology: please share a current network diagram (VPC/subnets, VPN/peering, NAT/egress points) and any firewalls that could affect long-lived TCP/TLS streams.
2) Egress path: where will traffic to Redwood's test endpoints egress? If traffic flows through a central egress NAT, we need the public IP ranges to allowlist and an estimate of concurrent connections allowed.
3) Latency budgets: internal application-to-proxy latency expectations (intra-VPC) - can you confirm typical RTTs between your app tier and the proposed inference host (or on-prem appliance)? We try to keep intra-VPC RTT < 10 ms and cross-region < 50 ms to meet SLOs.
4) VPN / Direct Connect / Peering: confirm whether you'll use site-to-site VPN, cloud peering, or Direct Connect; if VPN, please share tunnel IPs and expected throughput.
5) Test plan: we'd like to run a pre-cutover perf verification (synthetic load + streaming samples). Please indicate a contact from your networking/SRE team to coordinate packet captures, traceroutes, and a short window for a stress test.

Attachments: I've attached our SLO matrix and a blank network checklist to help you map the items above.

Next steps (proposed):
- Alex / Priya: share network diagram + contact for SRE/networking by EOD 6/25.
- Redwood (Marissa / Jordan / Neha): prepare perf test plan and runbook + share HubSpot deal link.
- Schedule 60-min network qualification call and a 2-hour perf verification window the following week.

Thanks - happy to adjust targets if you have constraints on VPN throughput or egress NAT concurrency.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
---
Attachments referenced: redwood-slo-matrix.pdf, network-checklist.xlsx

Thanks Marissa - great recap. We can share the network diagram and a point-of-contact from our SRE team (Priya Shah) by EOD today. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Egress: traffic will egress through a centralized NAT gateway in our VPC; we generally allow ~10k concurrent connections but we'll validate NAT timeouts for long-lived TLS streams.
- VPN / Peering: we currently have an AWS Direct Connect between our colo and primary cloud region; for the pilot we can open a peering/VPC endpoint to your test subnet if that helps reduce egress hops.

I'll attach a sanitized network diagram in my follow-up. Priya, can you confirm who on SRE will own traceroutes/pcaps for the verification run?

Appreciate the clear test plan, looking forward to the runbook.

- Alex
